# vendor/

Privately vendored copies of nice-plug and baseview, behind `[patch.crates-io]` in the root `Cargo.toml`. Lane FK of P1b made patches 1 to 5, lane FK2 patches 6 to 9, lane FK of FU1 patch 10, lane FK3 of R3 patch 11 and lane FK4 of R4/R5 patches 12 and 13; the fork lane owns this directory, and no other lane edits it (a lane that needs a change asks for it).

Why vendored and not a git fork: a public fork would expose the project's name, CI would depend on Codeberg being up, and `deny.toml` would need `allow-git`. Decision and measurements: `docs/adr/0001-plugin-shell.md` and `docs/adr/0002-ui-toolkit.md` (notes of 2026-10-19), research session `_local/sessions/2026-10-19-p1b-plugin-editor/`.

The directory is outside the cargo workspace (`exclude = ["vendor"]` in the root `Cargo.toml`), so `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy` and `--workspace` never touch it.

## Crates

Each package is the unchanged content of its crates.io `.crate` file at the version `Cargo.lock` pins. The bytes were taken from cargo's registry cache; each file's sha256 is the checksum `Cargo.lock` records (and the crates.io index serves), so they are the files crates.io hands out. Every entry keeps its crates.io version, so the exact `=` pins in the root `Cargo.toml` still match.

`nice-plug-derive` 0.1.2 and every other dependency stay on crates.io, unpatched.

Why egui-baseview is here: nice-plug-egui depends on it, and the keyboard-focus patch (4), the file-drop patch (11), the arrival-stamp patch (12) and the paste patch (13) edit it. A `[patch.crates-io]` entry replaces a crate everywhere in the graph, so baseview (under egui-baseview) is the vendored one too.

- nice-plug, nice-plug-core, nice-plug-egui: ISC, Copyright (c) 2022-2024 Robbert van der Helm. The crates.io packages carry no licence file; `LICENSE` in each of the three directories (added in the commit after the pristine import, the only file besides this README and `check-pristine.sh` that is not in a package) is the text of the repository's `LICENSE` at the Codeberg tag `v0.4.2` (fetched 2026-10-19).
- baseview, egui-baseview: `LICENSE-MIT` and `LICENSE-APACHE`, unchanged from the packages.
- Patch lines carry the licence of the crate they edit, so a human could still send them upstream.
- Entries in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`: the project distributes these crates (compiled in) with local changes, so the file records them with the changes.

## Lints

Cargo caps lints in registry dependencies (`--cap-lints allow`) but not in path dependencies, and `[patch.crates-io]` turns these five crates into path dependencies. CI builds with `CARGO_BUILD_WARNINGS=deny`, so any warning a vendored crate produces fails the build. Pristine nice-plug 0.4.2 already warns in release builds (`param_ptr` and `param_value` in `wrapper/state.rs` are used only inside a debug assertion), and a newer toolchain adds new warnings to every crate it compiles.

Each vendored `Cargo.toml` therefore ends with a `[lints.rust]` table that sets `warnings = "allow"` (the only edit to a manifest; `vendor/check-pristine.sh` shows it). nice-plug's table also declares `cfg(enth_rtsan)` (`unexpected_cfgs`, patch 10's RealtimeSanitizer instrumentation). That gives these crates what a crates.io dependency gets. The `[lints]` table is the per-crate form of an `#![allow(warnings, reason = "...")]`, and it needs no source edit. Hard errors a toolchain bump introduces are not covered: they need a patch.

When you edit vendored code, build once with the `warnings = "allow"` line removed from the crate you touched (keep nice-plug's `unexpected_cfgs` line), so that your own change is warning-free; then put the line back. Patch 10 was checked that way with `cargo clippy -p nice-plug` for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` and `aarch64-apple-darwin`: no warning. Patch 11 the same way with `cargo clippy -p egui-baseview` for the same three targets: no warning. Patches 12 and 13 showed that this is rustc's check only: `cargo clippy -p <crate>` from a workspace in which the crate is a `[patch]` path dependency (the root workspace, or a probe's) compiles it with plain rustc, because cargo hands clippy-driver workspace members only (a positive control in egui-baseview got rustc's `dead_code` warning and no `clippy::len_zero`). To run clippy's lints on a vendored crate, run it with the crate as its own workspace root, on a copy so that its `Cargo.lock` stays pristine: `cargo +1.99.1 clippy --offline --target <target> --config 'patch.crates-io.baseview.path="<repo>/vendor/baseview"'` in a copy of `vendor/egui-baseview` with the cap removed. Patches 12 and 13 were checked both ways for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` and `aarch64-apple-darwin`: no rustc warning (the `input-probe` build), and clippy's lints give the same 4 warnings with and without the two patches, all on older lines (`too_many_arguments` on `EguiWindow::new`, which patch 4's eighth argument set off, two `unnecessary_cast` and a `collapsible_if` in upstream's code).

Everything here is one git commit per change, after a single pristine-import commit. `git log --oneline -- vendor` is the list, and `vendor/check-pristine.sh` (`--full` for the whole diff) compares the tree with the `.crate` files in cargo's registry cache and checks their sha256 against the table above.

| 10 | nice-plug | **`is_main_thread()` never allocates.** In a host without CLAP's thread-check extension the CLAP wrapper answers `is_main_thread()` itself, and the VST3 wrapper always does (through the OS event loop); `schedule_gui()` asks it whenever `process()` schedules a GUI task: each parameter change (the editor is told), a voice-count change, a latency change. Upstream compared `std::thread::current().id()` under `permit_alloc` (a FIXME in `wrapper/clap/wrapper.rs`, `event_loop/linux.rs` and `event_loop/windows.rs`). On a thread where the plugin had not touched thread-local storage, the host's audio thread included, that allocated: glibc creates a `dlopen`ed library's TLS block for a thread on its first access (`__tls_get_addr` → `tls_get_addr_tail`, under `dl_load_tls_lock`, `malloc`; `elf/dl-tls.c`), and `thread::current()` builds a handle. A `thread_local!` of our own would allocate the same way (macOS creates a dylib's thread-locals lazily too). New `event_loop/os_thread.rs`: `OsThreadId` reads the identity the OS keeps in the thread's control block, with no TLS. Unix: `pthread_self()` and `pthread_equal()` (glibc: a load relative to the thread pointer, `%fs` or `tpidr_el0`, and `==`; `nptl/pthread_self.c`, `nptl/pthread_equal.c`, `sysdeps/{x86_64,aarch64}/nptl/tls.h`; Apple libpthread-539: TSD slot 0, `src/pthread_tsd.c`), through `libc` (Linux, BSDs) or declared against libSystem (macOS, where nice-plug has no `libc` dependency). Windows: `GetCurrentThreadId()`, declared against kernel32 (the `windows` crate's binding needs a feature nice-plug does not enable), the TEB's `ClientId` (Wine's `dlls/kernelbase/thread.c` reads it the same way). | 12 | egui-baseview | **Arrival stamps per event, and a keyboard claim for a tap pad.** egui sees input once per frame: `InputState::time` is the instant the frame took its input, so at 30 fps a key press can be up to about 33 ms older than its frame, and every event of the frame shares that time. `on_event` now takes an `Instant` before any work on a baseview event (on X11 baseview calls it from `drain_xcb_events` right after `poll_for_event` returns the event) and gives it to every egui event that event produced (a `Vec<Instant>` kept index for index with `RawInput::events`); each frame moves them into an `Arc<[Instant]>` and stores it, with the origin of `InputState::time`, in the context's temporary data under plain string keys (`egui::Id::unique("egui_baseview::arrival::stamps")`, an `Arc<[Instant]>` index for index with `InputState::raw.events`; `egui::Id::unique("egui_baseview::arrival::origin")`, an `Instant`), so that a crate that depends on egui alone (`enth-ui`) reads them without naming egui-baseview. New `arrival` module: `stamps(ctx)` (`None` when there are none or they do not line up with the pass's events: a second pass in one frame has no events), `origin(ctx)`, `events(ctx)` (each event with its instant), `egui_time(ctx, instant)`. `claim_keyboard(ctx, id)` (key `egui_baseview::keyboard_claim`, an `egui::Id`): under `KeyboardFocus::WhileTyping` the window takes the keyboard after a frame in which a widget that has egui's focus claimed it, exactly as for a focused text field (patch 4), and gives it back when the claim stops: Escape, a click elsewhere, the widget gone (egui's dead-man's switch), or another window taking the focus (patch 4's `Unfocused` handling takes egui's focus away, so the claim is not renewed and the editor does not take the keyboard back). A claim lasts one frame; under `OnClick` it does nothing. `window.rs` 81–104 (the claim), 424–425 and 534 (the stamps' field), 611–636 (`sync_keyboard_focus`), 753–775 (the frame stores the stamps), 944–945 and 1176–1179 (`on_event` stamps); `arrival.rs` (62 lines); `lib.rs` exports | 3 files, +129 / −3 | Not upstream: crates.io's latest egui-baseview is still 0.9.0 (2026-10-17, checked 2026-10-25 through the crates.io API), whose `on_event` keeps no time and whose focus follows clicks; the Codeberg repository was not re-read (its `robots.txt` disallows every path to AI agents' user agents), so the last look at `main` is FK3's of 2026-10-21 (`1f645a35d2`, the 0.9.0 commit). A design choice for enth's tap input ([ear.md](../docs/ear.md#rhythm-input)); the owner may propose it. Proof: `vendor/tests/input-probe/run.sh tap`, `tap-probe` under Xvfb with XTest, 19 of 19 checks directly and reparented: the claim (hover and a knob click leave Space to the host; a press on the pad takes the keyboard; Escape, a click elsewhere, the host taking the focus and the pad going away give it back, with no re-take over 12 frames) and the stamps of 24 mouse taps, 24 Space taps at gaps of 5 to 88 ms, 6 bursts of 4 taps 3 ms apart and 18 taps during 40 ms frames (every event of every frame stamped, each stamp after its XTest send and before its frame, none backwards, two taps in one frame apart by their sent gap within 0.33 ms). Measured (Xvfb, llvmpipe, a light editor, load 12 to 23): Space taps' lag from the XTest send to the stamp p50 0.19–0.27 / p95 0.24–2.2 ms, to the frame p50 15–16 / max 32 ms; the error of a tap interval p95 0.6–1.8 ms with stamps against 25–26 ms with frame times. **Limit:** a stamp is taken when the event loop reads the event, so an event that arrives while a frame is drawing waits for it: in 40 ms frames the lag reached 36–41 ms (p50 9–12) and the interval error p95 30–40 ms (frame times 43–59). Negative control for the claim: `tap-probe --no-claim` (the pad takes egui's focus, no claim), Space keeps reaching the host. The stamps have no build without the patch to compare with (no API upstream); each run compares them with the frame times upstream gives. `focus-probe` (patch 4, 11 and 6 checks per layout) and `drop-probe` (patch 11, 15 of 15) unchanged. The leak gate is unchanged with both patches: `cargo xtask leak-test` 14.12 KB per editor cycle (runs 13.78 and 14.12) against 14.14 (14.14, 14.05) on main `1c99e80` before them, limit 26, threads constant at 3; churn 0.35 against 0.46 KB per instance life. Not tested: Windows and macOS (clippy only; there the window gets events from the host's run loop, so a stamp also waits while the host's GUI thread is busy); REAPER and the real display (lane TAP's spike) |

## Tests

Everything here runs on a display only under Xvfb: the scripts unset `DISPLAY` and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and start `xvfb-run` themselves, and the programs that open windows refuse to run on a display that Xvfb does not serve. Builds take the shared build lock (`flock -s /tmp/enth-quiet.lock`) and at most 3 jobs. Each directory under `vendor/tests/` is its own cargo workspace outside the root workspace, with its own `Cargo.lock`, and patches the five crates to this directory.

- `vendor/check-pristine.sh`: the import (sha256 of each `.crate`, and the diff against it).
- `vendor/tests/editor-cycles/run.sh` (patches 2 and 3, about 9 minutes with a warm cache): `enth-test-host editor-cycles` with 200 cycles on a copy of spike-shell that counts `editor_closed()` calls, built twice: against this directory and against stock crates.io (`fork/`, `stock/`). The fork must call `editor_closed()` once per `build()`, keep the anonymous PSS growth within 26 KB per cycle over the baseline without an editor, and keep the thread count constant; the stock build is the negative control (no calls, about 84 KB per cycle).
- `vendor/tests/rename-check/run.sh` (patch 1): a plugin built on the vendored nice-plug and a small clack host that processes on its own thread, services `request_callback` and reads `clap_plugin_params.get_info` before and after. With the trigger it must see the name change and one `rescan(INFO | TEXT)`; without it (control) neither. `enth-test-host`'s `rescan` handler does nothing, so it cannot show this.
- `vendor/tests/focus-probe/run.sh` (patch 4): a program that plays a host window holding the X input focus, embeds the egui editor in it as a child, and drives mouse and keyboard through XTest. `while-typing` (11 checks) and `on-click` (upstream's behaviour, the negative control: Space is swallowed on hover and the focus stays after a click), each as a direct child and reparented the way the CLAP wrapper does it.
- `vendor/tests/drop-probe/run.sh` (patch 11, about 2 minutes warm): a host window with the egui editor embedded (directly, and created without a parent and reparented, the CLAP way) and, on its own X connection, an XDND version 5 drag source like a file manager's: it finds the outermost XdndAware window under the drop point (Qt's search from the root), owns `XdndSelection`, answers `ConvertSelection` with a `text/uri-list` and sends `XdndEnter`, `XdndPosition`, `XdndDrop` or `XdndLeave`. 15 checks: `[x11]`, what the source hears back (baseview's part), and `[egui]`, what egui sees in `hovered_files` and `dropped_files` (the patch's part). The fork must pass all of them (exit 0). The negative control is the same probe built against upstream egui-baseview 0.9.0, unpacked from the sha-checked `.crate` in cargo's registry cache (or against a git revision's `vendor/egui-baseview` with `--control-at REV`), through a command-line `[patch]`, which takes precedence over the manifest's: it must pass the `[x11]` checks and fail `[egui]` ones (exit 1). `drop-probe --into <title>` is a measurement for a host's plugin window on the same Xvfb: it lists the XdndAware windows and the plugin window's ancestors, then drops a WAV file at the plugin window's centre where a Qt-style source would and on the plugin window directly, and prints who asked for the data and who answered. `vendor/tests/drop-probe/reaper-into.sh [clap|vst3]` runs it against REAPER 7.82 (the sandbox and bundles `cargo xtask reaper-test --package enth-plugin` leaves, under Xvfb, with `reaper-into.lua` adding the plugin to a track and showing its window); it reports the project's item count before and after, and exits 0 when the run finished (a measurement, no pass or fail beyond that).
- `vendor/tests/input-probe/run.sh [tap|paste] [--control-at REV]` (patches 12 and 13, about 5 minutes warm): one crate, two probes, each with the egui editor embedded in a host window that holds the X input focus (`src/lib.rs`: the Xvfb guard, the host, XTest). `tap-probe` (patch 12; directly and reparented, with and without `--no-claim`) has a knob and a tap pad that takes egui's focus on a press and claims the keyboard; it checks the claim against patch 4 and the arrival stamps of XTest taps (every event stamped, each stamp after its send and before its frame, none backwards, taps in one frame apart, stamp intervals closer to the sent intervals than frame times), and prints the lags and interval errors (the Xvfb half of lane TAP's jitter table). `--no-claim` is the claim's negative control (Space must keep reaching the host); the stamps have no build without the patch (no API upstream), so each run compares them with the frame times. `paste-probe` (patch 13) owns `CLIPBOARD` on its own connection and counts every read: no read without Paste, one read and one `Event::Paste` per Paste click. Its negative control is the same probe built against upstream egui-baseview 0.9.0 (the sha-checked `.crate`) or a git revision (`--control-at REV`) through a command-line `[patch]`; only `paste-probe` is built for it (`tap-probe` needs patch 12's API), and it must fail (exit 1). The script exits 0 when every run ended as expected. Builds go to `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/input-probe` when that is set.
- Patch 5 is measured with `enth-test-host bursts --order both --capacity 1024` on spike-shell (`tools/test-host/proof.sh` runs the control).
- Patch 10 is measured with `cargo xtask rtsan` (nightly; `docs/plugin.md`, "RealtimeSanitizer"): its `no-thread-check` and `no-thread-check-bursts` scenarios run the test host without CLAP's thread-check extension (the default; `ENTH_TEST_HOST_THREAD_CHECK=1` offers it) and must be clean. The negative control is the same command on the tree before the fix (`git revert --no-commit` of the fix commit): both abort with exit 43. `OsThreadId` has a unit test in `os_thread.rs` (the crate's tests do not run from the root workspace; it was run as a standalone `rustc --test` against the `libc` rlib: 1 passed).
- Patches 6 to 9 are measured in REAPER (`xvfb-run -a cargo xtask reaper-test --package enth-plugin`, `docs/plugin.md`): `dirty-flag` (6), `state`'s `param-count` and `midi-cc-params` and the `mod-wheel` scenario (7), `param-renamed` (8), `macro-automation`'s `render-repeatable` (9). Patch 8 also keeps `vendor/tests/rename-check/run.sh` passing. The unit side is in `crates/enth-plugin` (`lib.rs` and `tests_host.rs`: the dirty and rescan requests, the VST3 controller list against what the plugin reads).
